lastCompletedStory.title: Wire model resolution into the run.ts orchestrator dispatch

nextStoryContext: src/commands/run.ts's setupPanes (the orchestrator dispatch site, the 4th and actually-last call site of the CAM-398 model-resolution epic -- discovered post-hoc as issue-398, after US-006's review.ts handoff prematurely claimed the epic closed at 3 sites) now calls resolvePhaseModel({ phase: 'orchestrator', backend: orchBackend, cacheReader: opts.codexModelsCacheReaderFn }) in place of the raw readPhaseModel('orchestrator', undefined, orchBackend) read, immediately where that read used to sit -- BEFORE the agentCmd = buildOrchestratorPaneCommand(...) argv build, and with no reorder of the pre-existing codexAuthPreflight block (still runs right before the orchestrator respawn-pane call, unchanged position, further down). A not-ok resolution returns setupPanes's SAME PRE-EXISTING { blocked: false } | { blocked: true; message: string } return shape the codexAuthPreflight not-proceed path already returns (message prefixed 'model-resolution-failed:'), propagating through setupOrchestratorSession up to runRun, which already surfaces result.blocked via the PRE-EXISTING printError('codex auth preflight failed', result.blocked) call -- this IS the escalation seam for this site (run.ts's orchestrator setup is a synchronous CLI path with NO escalateFn field on RunOptions at all, unlike loop.ts/plan-runner.ts/review.ts's async supervisor-loop dispatch closures; no new escalation plumbing was added). A new RunOptions.codexModelsCacheReaderFn?: CodexModelsCacheReader field (mirrors codexAuthCheckFn, doc comment alongside it) is the injectable seam, mirrored onto the internal SetupOpts interface and threaded through the setupOrchestratorSession({ ... codexModelsCacheReaderFn: options.codexModelsCacheReaderFn }) call in runRun; when absent, resolvePhaseModel's own default parameter (readCodexModelsCache) is used, and it is never invoked on a claude-backed dispatch. This site has NO configPath DI seam (unlike review.ts's pre-existing CAM-405 seam): readBackend()/resolvePhaseModel read scripts/cam/project.toml relative to process.cwd(), so the new test/commands/run-model-resolution.test.ts file needs the same mkdtempSync + process.chdir() fixture dance as run-codex-auth.test.ts's withCodexBackendCwd (here renamed withClaudeShapedCodexCwd, staging a claude-shaped flat [models] orchestrator = "sonnet" pin so the injected cache-reader seam actually fires, unlike run-codex-auth.test.ts's non-claude-shaped "gpt-5-codex" pin). This closes out the CAM-398 model-resolution wiring epic across all 4 dispatch call sites now known (loop.ts implementer [US-004], plan-runner.ts planner+auditor [US-005], review.ts reviewer [US-006], run.ts orchestrator [this story, US-007]) -- a future story reviving this thread would need a fresh audit of any NEW dispatch site added since, having learned from this story's own post-hoc discovery not to assert an epic is closed without an explicit dispatch-site grep sweep. src/commands/run.ts crossed its file-size ceiling (926->964, content.split('\n').length); raised in scripts/file-size-budget.json with a tracker-ref-carrying _ref entry, staged before the check:all re-run per the ratchet-gate rubric.

officialDocsValidated.summary: This story wires the already-built (US-003) resolvePhaseModel decision fn into the run.ts orchestrator dispatch call site; no new external library or documented API surface was introduced beyond what US-001..US-006 already Step-5.5-validated (Claude Code model-config docs, openai/codex protocol source, ~/.codex/models_cache.json schema).
